currentSprint.name: Vertical Slice 01 — Christian and The Dreamer
currentSprint.resumeNote: Dream v54 is gameplay-verified with scene-level backdrop/fog, continuous dusk sky, rear middle-distance dressing, tapered lantern glass, additive aura, bounded warm meadow falloff, bounded point-light pool, a feathered lantern warm-pool shader, one merged broken waymarker on the rear axis, subtle authored ground relief, softened ridge/fog continuity, distant outcrops occluded behind the ridge, bounded haze convergence on distant stone, v52 authored meadow zones, and a merged broken shrine silhouette behind the rear ridge. Fresh v52 critics score 7.6–7.8/10 front and 7.2–7.4/10 rear with artifact checks passing; the remaining quality gap is genuinely layered terrain/material depth. The v53 lit-state pool and v54 shrine still need visual captures because browser review is paused to protect workstation performance. Decoded audio calibration is browser-verified; native fallback now keeps footsteps audible without an AudioContext; physical-device listening and performance QA remain open. Verified release b2e61d1 is now live through the dist-only HTTPS deployment.

workstreams.critic: fresh live critic — fail, visual bar; gameplay contract now passes

workstreams.name: Delectable Mountains to Celestial City finale
workstreams.critic: focused real-controls finale smoke test — pass, 2.2m
workstreams.largestGap: Five new chapters complete Part One through the River and Celestial City with authored lighting, water, skyline, and watchfulness motifs. The remaining gap is a fresh visual critic pass and dedicated finale audio beds; River mobile tier is 96 draw calls p95 after its compact presentation.

workstreams.name: Mobile touch movement
workstreams.largestGap: Directional controls now capture the pointer and reset shared movement on up, cancel, lost capture, scene remount, modal pause, and player unmount; physical-device Safari gesture validation remains outstanding.

workstreams.name: Audio safety and browser unlock
workstreams.largestGap: Decoded scene beds and SFX now measure RMS/peak and receive bounded per-source calibration before the shared bus/master limiter; the title-screen journey action unlocks sound on first play, bounded native audio fallback covers Web Audio context/decode failures, native fallback footsteps use a wall-clock cadence, both Web Audio and native voices are capped at four concurrent transients, and AudioContext interruptions update the HUD and recover on gesture. Tests verify every resolved scene alias, SFX MP3 frame, native fallback footstep, first focus cue, and native voice cap. Dedicated finale compositions and physical-device listening QA remain outstanding.

workstreams.name: Performance and loading
workstreams.largestGap: Title now defers GameCanvas, keeping Three.js/Rapier out of the 252 KB production entry; the bundle guard requires a separate GameCanvas chunk under a 400 KB entry cap. Dream resource ownership now passes twelve repeated low-quality remount/release cycles with exactly-once disposal, City environment mounts sweep every owned root geometry while leaving shared palette materials alive, Chapter II's pure seedable definition factory derives all six landmark pads and every vegetation/rock rule is tested across canonical and alternate seeds for route/clearance/slope invariants, terrain tests lock deterministic ring topology and finite collider vertices, and persisted payloads reject null/empty numeric corruption while sanitizing replay indices, arrays, settings, onboarding flags, legacy completion migrations, final-beat-only chapter-complete handoffs, final-scene-final-beat game completion, non-finite replay steps, and puzzle flags against the current beat before lookup. `continueScene()`, choice responses, puzzle completion, and interaction callbacks now require their active progression state. Migration/merge helpers, resource disposal, first-step footsteps, first focus-puzzle audio playback, reload-at-complete behavior, malformed numeric preservation, replay-step clamping, early-completion rejection, replay-unlock rejection, transition gating, stale-modal rejection, missing-puzzle rejection, keyboard dialogue advancement, and the browser-free release gate are directly regression-tested. Gate remains 5.60s desktop / 4.44s mobile at 3.8 / 6.6 headless FPS with 124 / 88 draw-call p95; the new River finale tier is 7.06s desktop / 6.97s mobile at 142 / 96 draw-call p95 and 41,142 / 39,038 triangles. Hardware FPS, cold-start variance, and authored visual fidelity remain release blockers.
